metric.debugger_profiler_support.candidate_universe: Preserved candidate universe and findings from certified legacy work unit ecosystem-tooling--part-2--kotlin; recertification did not select a new language-specific target.

component_findings.advanced_debug: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-2--kotlin): When debugging Kotlin code, IntelliJ IDEA allows you to suspend the execution and diagnose problems that the code in coroutines may have. The debug information is available even if the coroutine is not running at the moment.
component_findings.basic_debug: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-2--kotlin): Kotlin inherits the full mature JVM debugger/profiler stack (IntelliJ debugger, JFR, async-profiler, YourKit, JProfiler, VisualVM) plus a dedicated first-party Coroutines debugger tab and Android Studio's dedicated CPU/Memory/Network/Energy profiler, with one documented rough edge around suspend-function variable visibility.
component_findings.cpu_profile: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-2--kotlin): Java Flight Recorder, built into the JDK since Java 11, provides low-overhead production profiling of CPU, memory allocation, GC, thread activity and I/O, and is recommended as the first tool for Kotlin profiling.
component_findings.integration_platforms: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-2--kotlin): One common issue is that variables used before calling a suspend function may be optimized out, making their values unavailable in the debugger.
component_findings.memory_profile: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-2--kotlin): Java Flight Recorder, built into the JDK since Java 11, provides low-overhead production profiling of CPU, memory allocation, GC, thread activity and I/O, and is recommended as the first tool for Kotlin profiling.

metric.debugger_profiler_support.limitations: Profiler/debugger maturity is largely inherited from the shared JVM/Android platform ecosystem rather than being Kotlin-specific tooling; this is consistent with Kotlin's design as a JVM-hosted language and is scored as accumulated ecosystem maturity per the metric definition, distinct from language-level debuggability scored under Language Quality.
metric.debugger_profiler_support.selection_rule: Evaluate implemented, documented debugging/profiling workflows on current supported toolchains; generic OS tools count only when language-aware use is documented.

metric.ide_editor_support_quality.candidate_universe: Preserved candidate universe and findings from certified legacy work unit ecosystem-tooling--part-2--kotlin; recertification did not select a new language-specific target.

component_findings.breadth_maintenance: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-2--kotlin): JetBrains provides official Kotlin support for the following IDEs and code editors: IntelliJ IDEA and Android Studio. You can also install the official Kotlin by JetBrains extension for Visual Studio Code, which is currently in Alpha. Other IDEs and code editors only have Kotlin community-supported plugins.
component_findings.completion_types: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-2--kotlin): IntelliJ IDEA is an IDE designed for JVM languages, such as Kotlin and Java, to maximize developer productivity. It does the routine and repetitive tasks for you by providing clever code completion, static code analysis, and refactorings.

component_findings.refactor_actions: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-2--kotlin): JetBrains provides official Kotlin support for the following IDEs and code editors: IntelliJ IDEA and Android Studio. You can also install the official Kotlin by JetBrains extension for Visual Studio Code, which is currently in Alpha. Other IDEs and code editors only have Kotlin community-supported plugins.
component_findings.syntax_navigation: Preserved paid evidence (ecosystem-tooling--part-2--kotlin): The VS Code extension is powered by the same Kotlin Language Server built on IntelliJ IDEA's code-insight infrastructure, and its Alpha feature set covers completion, diagnostics, navigation, quick-fixes, formatting, and project import.

metric.ide_editor_support_quality.limitations: Popularity/usage percentages cited in secondary sources (e.g., developer-preference percentages) are self-reported survey figures from third-party blogs and are used only as contextual color, not as the scoring basis.
metric.ide_editor_support_quality.selection_rule: Inspect the same editor capabilities across at least the dominant general-purpose editor and any major dedicated IDE when available.
